problem_statement: When a client socket is closed during an ongoing (asynchronous, non-blocking) TCP handshake, the TCP context is not immediately closed. The retransmission timer remains active, so SYN packets continue to be sent even after the socket is closed. If the server's IP later becomes reachable, a zombie TCP connection can be established that the application has no control over. The fix must ensure that closing a socket during an async handshake immediately tears down the TCP context, so no further SYN retransmissions occur and no connection is established after the socket is closed.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p qemu_x86 -T tests/net/socket/tcp -s tests/net/socket/tcp/net.socket.tcp -s net.socket.tcp -O twister-out --no-clean -W
